from: June book, night 11 (Saul Did Not Wait)
p1: Samuel told Saul, “Wait seven days, until I come.” Then Samuel would offer a sacrifice, a gift to the Lord. Those gifts helped people remember that Jesus would come.
Saul waited and waited. Enemies gathered close by, and many people went away. Saul felt worried and in a hurry.
After seven days, Samuel still had not come. So Saul did not wait any longer. He offered the gift himself.
p2: Just as Saul finished, Samuel came! Samuel asked, “What have you done?” He said Saul had not kept what the Lord commanded. The Lord wanted Saul to wait for His prophet.
Waiting can be hard, and Heavenly Father will help you wait. Waiting is one way to obey. Tonight, take three slow breaths and practice waiting.
old: Israel’s enemies were coming to attack! King Saul and his soldiers were scared. Samuel told Saul, “Wait seven days. I’ll come and make an offering to Heavenly Father for you.”
Saul waited. Day one, day two, day three... His soldiers started to leave because they were afraid! On day seven, Samuel still hadn’t come. Saul got impatient.
Saul said, “I can’t wait anymore!” He made the offering himself, even though only priests were supposed to do that. Right after he finished, Samuel arrived!
Samuel said, “You disobeyed! Because you didn’t wait and didn’t obey, you won’t be king forever. Heavenly Father will find someone else.” Saul’s impatience cost him everything.
